patterns.title: Drift to Low Performance
patterns.domain: Systems and feedback traps; eroding goals, adaptive standards, corrective effort, and operating capability

sources.author: Peter M. Senge
sources.title: The Fifth Discipline: The Art and Practice of the Learning Organization
sources.read_method: Opened the book text; read the eroding-goals discussion at PDF pages 94–95 and the Appendix 2 entry at PDF page 357. The scan identifies original 1990 copyright and 1994 paperback introduction.
sources.supports: Foundational terminology, two routes to reduce a gap, and eroding goals as a shifting-the-burden structure.
sources.boundary: Practical qualitative archetype, not a universal empirical law or proof that goal revisions are always wrong.

sources.author: Donella H. Meadows
sources.title: Thinking in Systems: A Primer
sources.read_method: Opened and read printed pages 121–123, PDF pages 137–139.
sources.supports: Title Drift to Low Performance; reinforcing erosion, perceived versus actual state, negative perception bias, and standard anchoring.
sources.boundary: Qualitative structural account. The article qualifies rigid and best-ever standards using feasibility and resource constraints. The frog anecdote is not used as factual evidence.

sources.author: Virginia Anderson
sources.title: Introducing the Systems Archetypes: Drifting Goals
sources.read_method: Opened and read full practitioner article; PDF edition dated October 1999. Adapted from Kim and Anderson, Systems Archetype Basics (1998).
sources.supports: Corrective action delay, goal adjustment, and explicit distinction between legitimate adaptation and erosion.
sources.boundary: Practitioner explanation; its Tato Bits narrative is not treated as empirical evidence.

sources.author: Daniel H. Kim
sources.title: Drifting Goals: The Challenge of Conflicting Priorities
sources.read_method: Opened the article and PDF edition; read quality/schedule conflicts and interdependent-goal discussion. PDF edition dated November 1999.
sources.supports: Rigid deadlines without needed resources can shift degradation to quality; multiple interdependent requirements must be considered.
sources.boundary: Practical qualitative analysis, not an estimated policy effect.

sources.author: Rogelio Oliva and John D. Sterman
sources.title: Death Spirals and Virtuous Cycles: Human Resource Dynamics in Knowledge-Based Services
sources.read_method: Opened author-uploaded chapter; read model introduction, work-pressure/effort response, Erosion of service standards, and discussion of capacity and simulated policy behavior.
sources.supports: Field-informed modeling of service norms and asymmetric adjustment, explicitly referring to their 2001 UK bank study.
sources.boundary: Field-based calibration and simulation are distinguished. No coefficient or staffing-effect estimate is transferred to the hypothetical support service. This chapter is a primary authored account of their modeling work, not a controlled general-population test.

patterns.short_description: Identify when disappointing results are lowering the standard used to judge them, then reconnect the standard to its purpose and fund a feasible path toward it.
use_when: Did service improve, or did the standard move?
goals: Recognize the familiar situation and preserve the defining mechanism.
Distinguish formal assumptions, empirical findings, and hypothetical continuations.
Make intervention authority, opportunity costs, and remaining constraints explicit.
mechanisms: Separate forecasts from the justified service promise and resource a feasible recovery.
A target adds no capacity. Training, backlogs, changing needs, and unaffordable promises require explicit decisions.

example_structure.scenario: Support response standard is relaxed after misses; unchanged waiting looks more acceptable, recovery loses priority, waiting worsens, and further relaxation follows. Forecasts and justified service promises have different roles. Actual waits and target history must be tracked independently. Real coverage, backlog, demand, training, and legitimate scope revision remain material; no numerical trajectory or inevitable decline asserted.

example_structure.residual_constraints: A target adds no capacity. Training, backlogs, changing needs, and unaffordable promises require explicit decisions.
example_structure.comparison: Qualitative choices, dependencies, and consequences; no invented scores, computed trajectory, or measured improvement claimed.
